sources.entry: Documize - Modern Docs + Wiki software with built-in workflow, single binary executable, just bring MySQL/Percona. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Go

summary.one_liner: Documize Community is a self-hosted, open source knowledge management and wiki platform built with Go and EmberJS, shipped as a single executable binary.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Documize as a self-hosted knowledge management solution aimed at both technical and non-technical users, for customer-facing and internal documentation. Content is organized through labels, spaces and categories. It is built with Golang and EmberJS and compiled to a single executable for Linux, Windows and macOS, with Raspberry Pi (ARM) builds also listed. The user supplies an external database: PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, or a MySQL variant such as Percona or MariaDB, all of which require full-text search support. Login can be email/password, or LDAP, Active Directory, Red Hat Keycloak, or CAS, with optional dual authentication alongside email/password for LDAP/AD. The interface is localized into several languages. The README also describes a paid Community+ edition with approval workflows, versioning, PDF export, audit logs and other enterprise features.
use_cases: single-binary docs server on Linux, Windows or macOS
notable: Compiled to a single executable binary with no separate runtime required beyond the database
Supports PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server/Azure, MySQL, Percona and MariaDB
LDAP, Active Directory, Keycloak and CAS authentication with optional dual login
Localized into nine languages out of the box
Community+ paid edition adds approval workflows, versioning and audit logs
caveats: Full-text search support is mandatory for every database type
Advanced features such as approval workflows, PDF export and audit logs are only in the paid Community+ edition, which is free for the first five users and priced from $900 per year for 100 users
The README does not include install or run instructions
